summary: The [digital agenda launched in 2019](2022-03-27-guinea-ecuatorial-adige-agenda-digital) on 33 lines of action ran to 2025 and has produced no implementation report, budget figure or successor.
developments:
It was aligned with three international frameworks and is the agenda a World Bank diagnostic assesses against, with the diagnostic's recommendations outstanding ([diagnostic](2024-06-25 Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Country Diagnostic - Bridging the Gaps), [priority actions](2024-07-15 World Bank identifies priority actions for DPI in Equatorial Guinea)).

The national development strategy to 2035 commits to gradual privatisation of state telecom ownership, a universal broadband backbone across all regions, an updated telecoms legal framework and a science and innovation fund that may be financed by a special tax on oil and gas exports; the diagnostic's own digital recommendations, a one-stop shop, online business registration and a digitised commercial registry, remain undelivered ([strategy text](2024-05-01-guinea-ecuatorial-ends-2035-estrategia-desarrollo-sostenible), [economic memorandum](2025-03-04 Country Economic Memorandum on Equatorial Guinea 2025 - Building Foundations for Renewed Diversified and Inclusive Growth)).

A consolidated action plan for the second half of 2026 was adopted in July with 35 strategic objectives under three national priorities, one of them restoring sovereignty over the national digital space; it is not yet financed and goes to the Council of Ministers, which decides what is recorded and funded ([action plan](2026-07-31-guinea-ecuatorial-consejo-directivo-ministerio-transportes-dominio-gq)).

summary: An [international tender to draft a replacement telecommunications law](2025-06-04-reforma-ley-telecomunicaciones-licitacion-ahoraeg) opened in June 2025 and has produced no award, draft or revised timetable.
developments:
The tender was scoped to cover artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, satellite connectivity and data protection ([tender](2025-06-04-reforma-ley-telecomunicaciones-licitacion-ahoraeg)).

Fourteen months on, the 2005 statute still governs a sector that has since acquired a second state operator, an offshore satellite authorisation and a directorate for artificial intelligence, none of which it contemplates.

summary: A [negotiating commission is to be created](2026-07-31-guinea-ecuatorial-consejo-directivo-ministerio-transportes-dominio-gq) to recover the country-code domain from a foreign operator the release does not name.
developments:
The commission was named in the July to December 2026 plan ([plan](2026-07-31-guinea-ecuatorial-consejo-directivo-ministerio-transportes-dominio-gq)).

Nothing is established about the current administration arrangement, so the base holds an intention to recover a domain and no statement of who holds it or on what terms. No cloud or storage policy exists beside it.

summary: [Ley 7/2024 on social media and computer crime](2026-07-02-ley-7-2024-redes-sociales-menores-privacidad-ahoraeg) has been in force since December 2024, its full text unheld and its provisions known from reporting.
developments:
Its provisions were reported in rollout from July 2026 ([the law](2026-07-02-ley-7-2024-redes-sociales-menores-privacidad-ahoraeg)).

The same statute creates the national cybersecurity and critical infrastructure agency under the Presidency, and that body has no premises, staffing, budget or activity on record, so the law's institutional half exists only on paper.

summary: The [cybersecurity agency created by statute](2026-07-02-ley-7-2024-redes-sociales-menores-privacidad-ahoraeg) has no premises, staffing, budget or activity on record.
developments:
It was created by the December 2024 law under the Presidency ([creation](2026-07-02-ley-7-2024-redes-sociales-menores-privacidad-ahoraeg)).

No incident response team, sector designation, audit programme or national strategy exists anywhere in the base, so an agency named in a statute is the whole of the country's cybersecurity institutional record.

summary: [Ley 1/2016](2016-07-22-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-1-2016-proteccion-datos-personales) has been in force since August 2016, giving rights of access, rectification, cancellation and opposition and a sanctions regime to CFA 15,000,000.
developments:
It was gazetted on 22 July 2016 and took effect twenty days later ([the law](2016-07-22-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-1-2016-proteccion-datos-personales)).

Ten years on, no implementing decree, guidance or enforcement action under it is held, and the country signed the continental convention on the same subject only in July 2026.

summary: The [supervisory body the statute provides for was never created](2016-07-22-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-1-2016-proteccion-datos-personales): article 15 leaves it to a decree the government has not issued.
developments:
The article leaves both the supervisory organ and the registry it would run to that decree, and a continental country register records no supervisory authority publicly identified ([the law](2016-07-22-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-1-2016-proteccion-datos-personales)).

So a statute with a sanctions regime running to CFA 15,000,000 ([the law](2016-07-22-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-1-2016-proteccion-datos-personales)) has had no body able to apply it for ten years, which is the clearest instance on this ledger of a law without an institution.

summary: A [draft artificial intelligence law](2025-08-27-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-inteligencia-artificial-aniad) is being written, setting six guiding principles and proposing an autonomous national authority for the technology and for data.
developments:
A drafting session in August 2025 addressed splitting the proposed authority's functions, and two national institutions are named as prospective training and certification centres under the draft; no enactment, text or adoption date is published ([draft law](2025-08-27-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-inteligencia-artificial-aniad)).

The proposed authority would supervise both artificial intelligence and data, in a country whose existing data-protection statute has had no supervisory body for a decade.

summary: A [reform of the 1997 press law](2026-08-07-eqguinea-parliament-digital-communications-mining-bills) was presented in August 2026, regulating digital media and cable television for the first time.
developments:
It was referred to a parliamentary committee alongside a separate copyright and related rights bill implementing the country's convention obligations; neither bill text is held and no adoption date is published ([presentation](2026-08-07-eqguinea-parliament-digital-communications-mining-bills), [scope](2026-08-07-gnq-ley-prensa-medios-digitales)).

A commission adopted 11 articles of the draft on 18 August 2026, leaving four outstanding, on the principles of the profession, the qualification required to practise, student interns, and professional secrecy; no plenary vote, text or commencement date is published ([commission stage](2026-08-19-realeg-gnq-ley-prensa-comision-once-articulos)).

summary: The country [signed the continental cyber and data convention](2026-07-29-equatorial-guinea-signs-malabo-convention-au-commission) on 28 July 2026 and is not a party to it.
developments:
No instrument of ratification is on file or on the continental register ([signature](2026-07-29-equatorial-guinea-signs-malabo-convention-au-commission)).

The Chamber of Deputies' unanimous vote of 25 March 2026 was a domestic authorisation to ratify, taken four months before the country became a signatory, so the two acts ran in the wrong order and the second has not followed ([authorisation](2026-03-25-ratifican-convencion-malabo-ciberseguridad-datos-reg)).

summary: The country [took part in a regional data governance workshop](2026-07-28-advancing-data-infrastructure-and-governance-in-lusophone-africa) in June 2026 applying an international toolkit, with no national framework resulting.
developments:
It was the second such workshop in the Lusophone Africa process ([workshop](2026-07-28-advancing-data-infrastructure-and-governance-in-lusophone-africa)).

No commitment, framework or follow-up is recorded from it, and it is the only regional policy process the base holds outside the continental convention and a bilateral accord with one neighbour.

The central bank adopted a regional financial inclusion strategy for 2025-2029 covering the six member states, validated by the monetary union's ministerial committee on 21 December 2023 and published in February 2025 ([strategy](2025-02-01-beac-strategie-regionale-inclusion-financiere-cemac)); the base holds no member-state implementation plan, target or outturn under it.

summary: [Three accords with Gabon](2025-11-13-gabon-guinea-ecuatorial-fibra-roaming-frecuencias-techafricanews) were signed in November 2025 covering fibre interconnection, free roaming and frequency coordination.
developments:
No traffic or tariff figure is published ([accords](2025-11-13-gabon-guinea-ecuatorial-fibra-roaming-frecuencias-techafricanews)).

The July 2026 connectivity plan separately names a zero-roaming arrangement with four neighbours, so the roaming half of the accords has a stated regional extension and no measurement at either end.

summary: A [border-screening connection](2024-01-01 I-CEMAC (INTERPOL border-management project, Central Africa)) runs at ten sites including three airports, with no traffic figure and no successor project.
developments:
It was extended under a regional border-management project running to 2024 ([connection](2024-01-01 I-CEMAC (INTERPOL border-management project, Central Africa))).

It is the only cross-border data exchange the base holds, and no data-protection arrangement, retention rule or oversight applies to it on the record, in a country whose own supervisory body was never constituted.

summary: A [service-quality regulation](2026-08-10-guinea-ecuatorial-ortel-reglamentos-index) of 2018 is confirmed in force through the regulator's own index, with only its title and date held.
developments:
The index also lists an inspection and sanctions regulation of 2020 and a broadband-market update of February 2026, neither captured separately ([regulatory index](2026-08-10-guinea-ecuatorial-ortel-reglamentos-index)).

So the country has published quality-of-service rules and the base cannot read them; no measurement, inspection outcome or sanction under any of the three is held.

summary: The telecommunications ministry's vote [fell 23 per cent to CFA 5,802,246 thousand for 2026](2025-12-09-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-presupuestos-generales-estado-2026), 0.4 per cent of the total budget.
developments:
The prior year's figure was CFA 7,556,246 thousand, and the 2026 vote includes CFA 140,000 thousand for the telecommunications school at the new capital, against a total budget of CFA 1,294,282m ([budget law](2025-12-09-guinea-ecuatorial-ley-presupuestos-generales-estado-2026)).

It is the only domestic appropriation for the sector the base holds at any date, and it fell in the year the ministry adopted a 35-objective plan it states is not yet financed.

summary: Two Chinese policy-bank facilities, [US$402m for a submarine cable](2015-01-01-eximbank-cn-gnq-001-china-eximbank-provides-402-million-buyers) and [US$70.3m for video surveillance](2019-01-01-cdb-gnq-001-cdb-provides-703-million-loan-for), carry no repayment or delivery record.
developments:
The cable credit is drawn and the cable is in service, with no repayment or restructuring on record ([cable credit](2015-01-01-eximbank-cn-gnq-001-china-eximbank-provides-402-million-buyers)).

The surveillance loan is committed, with no delivery, siting or oversight arrangement for the system on record ([surveillance loan](2019-01-01-cdb-gnq-001-cdb-provides-703-million-loan-for)).

Together they are the only external project financing the base holds for the sector, and neither has a disbursement or completion statement against it.

summary: The country lands [three submarine systems](2018-06-06 Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon are now more connected - AFR-IX telecom) and has two more under study or agreement, with no capacity or utilisation figure for any of them.
developments:
One regional system was inaugurated in 2018 on a 400 km route between the two main cities and a neighbour, alongside an earlier landing; no later capacity or utilisation figure is held ([regional cables](2018-06-06 Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon are now more connected - AFR-IX telecom)).

The state infrastructure operator is landing party for the continental system and hosted its maintenance committee in May 2026, with capacity unchanged on the record ([landing party](2026-05-06-gitge-anfitrion-consorcio-ace-reg)).

A Mediterranean-anchored system is under study at a landing in one of two towns, put at EUR 20-60m and 2029 to 2030 with an alternative route also named, the existing cable reported to degrade quality which is the stated reason for diversifying ([study](2026-04-03-estudio-cable-submarino-medusa-analysys-mason-reg), [routes](2026-06-05-cables-submarinos-africa-medusa-via-africa-larazon)).

A subsea fibre agreement with Nigeria was signed in February 2026 bundling a data centre, with no route, capacity or delivery date published ([agreement](2026-02-24 Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea subsea cable strengthens connectivity), [signature](2026-02-12-nigeria-equatorial-guinea-subsea-fibre)).

summary: A [semestral plan targets 85 per cent second- and fourth-generation coverage](2026-07-31-guinea-ecuatorial-consejo-directivo-ministerio-transportes-dominio-gq) through 34 new towers in the islands and the interior.
developments:
The plan was presented to the Prime Minister in July 2026 and also names a zero-roaming arrangement with four neighbours and a national digital postcode system; the plan document itself is not held ([connectivity plan](2026-07-31-guinea-ecuatorial-consejo-directivo-ministerio-transportes-dominio-gq)).

No current coverage figure, subscription series or penetration rate is published at any date, so the 85 per cent target ([plan](2026-07-31-guinea-ecuatorial-consejo-directivo-ministerio-transportes-dominio-gq)) has no starting point on the record.

summary: A satellite service was [authorised temporarily for offshore operations](2026-07-28-guinea-ecuatorial-autoriza-starlink-empresas-norteamericanas-alta-mar) in July 2026, with extension to individual subscribers deferred on security grounds.
developments:
The authorisation covers North American companies' offshore operations inside jurisdictional waters and was signed at the presidential palace on 28 July 2026 ([authorisation](2026-07-28-guinea-ecuatorial-autoriza-starlink-empresas-norteamericanas-alta-mar)).

Type-approval and competences remain unresolved with the regulator ([implementation](2026-07-29-ahoraeg-starlink-ortel-implementacion)), against an entry signalled in February 2025 that was not then authorised ([entry](2025-02-21-starlink-implantarse-conectividad-reg)).

So the service is lawful for foreign companies at sea and unlawful for citizens on land, which is the sharpest statement of access policy the base holds.

summary: A [tender was published](2026-06-03-pamfp-licitacion-centros-datos-malabo-bata-reg) for a primary data centre in one city and a solar-powered backup in the other, for public financial data.
developments:
It follows data-economy actions including data centres validated with the World Bank in December 2025 ([validation](2025-12-19-banco-mundial-valida-economia-digital-datacenter-reg)), and covers storage, processing and backup ([tender](2026-06-03-pamfp-licitacion-centros-datos-malabo-bata-reg)).

What exists today is two technical facilities described in the state operator's own factsheet, one in each city, each with two generators and ten nodes with distribution and transmission equipment; no floor-area, power or storage figure is given, and the document's content narrates 2016 and 2017 work despite a 2025 upload path ([factsheet](2025-07-01-gitge-informe-anual)).

summary: A [digital economic zone](2026-03-27-zeede-djibloho-zona-economica-digital-reg) at the new capital is under evaluation around artificial intelligence, big data and high-performance data centres.
developments:
No instrument, site or investment figure is published ([zone](2026-03-27-zeede-djibloho-zona-economica-digital-reg)).

No commercial data centre exists anywhere in the base, so the whole of the private-capacity record is a zone under evaluation and a data centre bundled into a subsea cable agreement with Nigeria.

summary: A [proposal to replace copper with fibre in electrical substations](2026-05-22-guinea-ecuatorial-segesa-fibra-optica-modernizacion) was presented in May 2026, for fault prediction and reduced fire risk.
developments:
The state electricity company and a foreign vendor would lease spare capacity to telecom operators to extend national broadband coverage; it is under review, the Vice-President citing a need for exhaustive analysis before viability is determined ([proposal](2026-05-22-guinea-ecuatorial-segesa-fibra-optica-modernizacion)).

It remains a proposal rather than a contract, and the base holds no power supply position for network sites or data centres at any date, against two data centres under tender.

summary: No [interoperability framework](2026-08-07-eqguinea-national-development-agency-data-silos) exists, and the development agency names limited data-sharing by line ministries as its main obstacle to monitoring delivery.
developments:
The absence was named by the World Bank diagnostic and no framework, standard or governing body has been published since ([diagnostic](2024-06-25 Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Country Diagnostic - Bridging the Gaps), [priority actions](2024-07-15 World Bank identifies priority actions for DPI in Equatorial Guinea)).

At the agency's directorship handover on 7 August 2026, its outgoing Inspector General stated the consequence directly: limited sharing by line ministries is what stops it monitoring delivery against the national development strategy ([handover](2026-08-07-eqguinea-national-development-agency-data-silos)).

progress: No change, a first measurement with no earlier figure behind it
summary: A study puts ministry [interoperability at about 15 per cent, big data at 21 and data analysis at 10](2026-07-02-estudio-gitge-brecha-transformacion-digital-ministerios-ecofinge).
developments:
The measurement is the state infrastructure operator's own, published in July 2026 ([study](2026-07-02-estudio-gitge-brecha-transformacion-digital-ministerios-ecofinge)).

It is the only assessment of government systems anywhere in the base, no earlier reading exists to measure direction against, and the three figures are consistent with the development agency's own account of ministries that do not share data.

summary: The [biometric identity document](2025-04-04 Government wants a rigorous control mechanism for issuing the literal (birth) certificate) is issued from a central agency, with a 2025 national tour reporting 7,670 dossiers obtained and 7,275 processed.
developments:
Issuance takes about 30 days for the identity document and 14 to 17 days for a passport, and the tour figures remain the most recent held ([tour](2025-04-04 Government wants a rigorous control mechanism for issuing the literal (birth) certificate), [agency](2024-01-01 On the functioning of Equatorial Guinea's National Centre for the Issuance of Official Documents (CNEDOGE))).

The executive has invited parents to register children and adults over 18 to obtain the document ([invitation](2024-03-15 The Executive invites parents to register children in the Civil Registry and adults over 18 to obtain the DIP)).

There is no digital identity: the World Bank diagnostic records a 2018 digital civil-registry pilot only and recommends building one, and nothing has been built since ([diagnostic](2024-05-18 Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Diagnostic (World Bank full report))).

summary: The [civil registry remains paper-based](2025-06-17-reunion-africana-crvs-sipopo-reg), with a 2018 digital pilot and fraudulent birth certificates identified as a control problem.
developments:
The country hosted the continental civil-registration meeting in June 2025 and no digitisation milestone or registration coverage figure has followed ([meeting](2025-06-17-reunion-africana-crvs-sipopo-reg)).

The government has stated it wants a rigorous control mechanism for issuing birth certificates, which is the same document the identity document depends on ([control mechanism](2025-04-04 Government wants a rigorous control mechanism for issuing the literal (birth) certificate)).

summary: Two wallets launched in 2026, on a base holding [0.41 per cent of regional payment volume](2026-04-08-beac-rapport-services-paiement-cemac-2024), the smallest share of six member states.
developments:
The share is measured at end-2024 by the regional central bank ([regional report](2026-04-08-beac-rapport-services-paiement-cemac-2024)).

A bank wallet launched in February 2026 with a payment service and a prepaid card, with no user or transaction figure published ([bank wallet](2026-02-12-bange-mobile-ge-app-reg)).

The state operator named a wallet of its own as part of its modernisation, again with no user or transaction figure ([operator wallet](2026-05-25-getesa-modernizacion-5g-wifi-getesa-money-reg)).

summary: [No mobile-money licensing decision is on record](2026-03-29-fintech-ecosystem-2026-thefintechtimes), and bank and telecom applications have launched without one being reported.
developments:
The absence of a licensed operator was named by the World Bank diagnostic and nothing has changed it ([diagnostic](2024-06-25 Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Country Diagnostic - Bridging the Gaps)).

Two wallets nonetheless entered service during 2026 ([market account](2026-03-29-fintech-ecosystem-2026-thefintechtimes)), so services are running ahead of the authorisation that would govern them, which is the same pattern as the data-protection statute without its supervisory body.

summary: Five commercial banks and the regional central bank were [pressed to expand cash machines, terminals and card issuance](2026-02-25-vp-banca-cajeros-tpv-pago-electronico-reg) in February 2026.
developments:
The expansion is sought for value-added tax control and tourism, and no deployment count has been published ([pressure](2026-02-25-vp-banca-cajeros-tpv-pago-electronico-reg)).

A national plan for cash machines and terminals was launched in May 2025, with connectivity named by the banks and the state infrastructure operator as the limiting factor ([plan](2025-05-27-plan-nacional-cajeros-tpv-identicge)).

So the country has a plan, a ministerial push and no count of machines or terminals at either date.

summary: A [treasury single account](2026-08-05-el-gobierno-impulsa-la-implementacion-de-la-cuenta-unica-del-tesoro) has a five-phase roadmap adopted and production targeted for the first quarter of 2027, with the annual tax licence already filed online.
developments:
A census of all state bank accounts is complete and the account is to be built on the regional central bank's own systems, with no cost, agency or supplier stated ([roadmap](2026-08-05-el-gobierno-impulsa-la-implementacion-de-la-cuenta-unica-del-tesoro)).

The single tax licence moved online in January 2026, with no transaction or take-up figure published ([tax licence](2026-01-12-digitalizacion-patente-tributaria-unica-reg)).

summary: An [electronic logistics system for malaria commodities](2022-12-08 Deploying DHIS2 for eLMIS to improve Malaria stock management in Equatorial Guinea) runs on one island, with no extension beyond it on record.
developments:
It was deployed under a malaria elimination programme ([deployment](2022-12-08 Deploying DHIS2 for eLMIS to improve Malaria stock management in Equatorial Guinea)).

It is the only health information system in the base, it covers one commodity class on one island, and no national health management information system, facility count or coverage figure exists.

summary: The document agency [opened two provincial offices with online appointment booking](2026-06-12-cnedoge-nuevas-oficinas-citas-online-ahoraeg), and a civil-service management system is in implementation.
developments:
The offices opened in June 2026 at two interior cities, with booking through the agency's own site, where citizens had previously travelled to central offices ([offices](2026-06-12-cnedoge-nuevas-oficinas-citas-online-ahoraeg), [tariffs](2025-04-02-cnedoge-camara-diputados-tarifas-documentos-ahoraeg)).

An administrative-procedure tracker launched in 2021 lets citizens follow a procedure's status through the public service ministry's site, with no processing-time or usage figure published in five years ([tracker](2021-06-18-guinea-ecuatorial-sigob-lanzamiento)).

A civil-service management system with biometric attendance and automated payroll is in implementation on an estimated eighteen-month timeline, with a steering committee convened in March 2026 and a monitoring strategy ([steering committee](2026-03-04-sigf-comite-pilotaje-m2m-ahoraeg), [timeline](2026-02-20-sigf-activa-funcion-publica-18-meses-reg)).

summary: The country holds a [state secretariat](2026-07-07-oscar-ondo-ngomo-asume-secretario-estado-ia-realeg) and a director-general for artificial intelligence, neither with a published mandate, budget or workplan.
developments:
The secretariat was first named at secretary-of-state level in August 2024 and changed hands in July 2026 under a decree of 23 June ([first appointment](2024-08-23-decreto-86-2024-secretarios-estado-guinea-ecuatorial), [current decree](2026-06-25-decreto-61-2026-secretarios-estado-guinea-ecuatorial), [handover](2026-07-07-oscar-ondo-ngomo-asume-secretario-estado-ia-realeg)).

A director-general for the technology sits within the transport and telecommunications ministry, again with no published mandate, budget or workplan for the directorate ([directorate](2026-07-23-guinea-ecuatorial-equacom-avante-debate-transformacion-digital), [public-sector programme](2025-08-27-pnud-digital-fitness-sector-publico-undp)).

Two named offices, a draft law and a proposed authority, and no deployed system, dataset, compute facility or use-case register anywhere in the base.

progress: Mixed, board appointments were opened to competition while a second state operator's merger was halted for an audit
summary: Parastatal directorships were [filled by competitive interview](2026-07-30-guinea-ecuatorial-evaluacion-aspirantes-cargos-directivos-gitge-inseso), and the second state operator's merger is [halted pending an audit](2026-07-23-guinea-ecuatorial-regimen-incompatibilidades-empresas-publicas-telgesa).
developments:
Article 16 of the public enterprises law was invoked to remove supervising officeholders from parastatal boards, and director-general posts at four state companies were filled by competitive interview against stated criteria ([appointments](2026-07-30-guinea-ecuatorial-evaluacion-aspirantes-cargos-directivos-gitge-inseso), [incompatibility regime](2026-07-23-guinea-ecuatorial-regimen-incompatibilidades-empresas-publicas-telgesa)).

The state infrastructure operator is now led by a new director-general and deputy after that process, replacing one of thirteen years' standing; the new leadership's first recorded act was a meeting with its Chinese equipment supplier on collaboration strategies, with no contract, scope or value attached ([new leadership](2026-08-18-real-equatorial-la-nueva-directiva-de-gitge-y), [handover](2026-08-07-gitge-inicia-una-nueva-etapa-con-salvador-nguema-funtam-al-frente)).

The second state operator, announced at about US$50m with 260 towers and 90 per cent coverage, has had its merger with a foreign group halted until an audit establishes the assets, liabilities and debts of the company being merged ([halt](2026-07-15-huawei-rescatar-getesa-telgesa-radiomacuto)).

summary: A [digital transformation forum](2026-07-23-guinea-ecuatorial-avante-actores-tic-transformacion-digital) convened in July 2026 naming artificial intelligence, electronic payments and public-administration reform as its three priority axes.
developments:
It was backed by the national development agency ([forum](2026-07-23-guinea-ecuatorial-avante-actores-tic-transformacion-digital)).

It is the only convening of the technology sector the base holds, and no hub, incubator, accelerator or workspace appears anywhere in the record.

summary: A [digital marketplace](2026-08-19-ahora-eg-okoume-se-presenta-oficialmente-en-malabo) launched in August 2026 as a structured replacement for the messaging groups that carry much of the country's informal commerce.
developments:
It was launched before ministers by its founder; it is a private platform and no user count, payment integration or regulatory status is published ([marketplace](2026-08-19-ahora-eg-okoume-se-presenta-oficialmente-en-malabo)).

A separate platform is named by the ministry as the national electronic commerce platform, on which small firms, traders and farmers are to be trained to open free online stores, and is organising the country's first electronic commerce and digital payments workshop for September and October 2026; no ownership, transaction volume, merchant count or launch date for the platform itself is stated ([national platform](2026-08-14-eqguinea-selba24-ecommerce-seminar)).

summary: A [technology institute trains more than 200 students](2025-06-17-china-apoyo-desarrollo-tecnologico-ahoraeg) with Chinese universities under a cooperation roadmap.
developments:
No later enrolment or graduation figure is on record ([training](2025-06-17-china-apoyo-desarrollo-tecnologico-ahoraeg)).

It is the only training institution the base names, and the draft artificial intelligence law would make it and the national university prospective certification centres, so a single institute carries both the current provision and the planned one.

summary: A [digital transformation and cybersecurity programme](2025-08-27-pnud-digital-fitness-sector-publico-undp) for multisectoral officials was delivered once in August 2025 and not repeated.
developments:
No later cohort, participant count or evaluation is on record ([programme](2025-08-27-pnud-digital-fitness-sector-publico-undp)).

It is the only civil-service training the base holds, against a civil-service management system now in implementation and a ministry maturity study that puts data-analysis capability in the low single figures.

summary: [Doctoral findings on big data, interoperability and digital identity](2026-07-23-guinea-ecuatorial-equacom-avante-debate-transformacion-digital) were presented at the July 2026 forum, the only national research on record.
developments:
No research programme, funding line or publication is held ([presentation](2026-07-23-guinea-ecuatorial-equacom-avante-debate-transformacion-digital)).

The national development strategy proposes a science, technology and innovation fund that may be financed by a special tax on oil and gas exports, and that fund does not exist, so one doctoral presentation is the whole of the research record.

summary: The [fifth population census and a first agricultural census](2026-08-20-ahoraeg-comite-cientifico-censo-poblacion-agropecuario) had their strategic documents validated in August 2026, with no enumeration date published.
developments:
Both run together under a decree of March 2025, with scientific committees created by a resolution of April 2025, and the last population census was in 2015 ([validation](2026-08-20-ahoraeg-comite-cientifico-censo-poblacion-agropecuario)).

The validated project document is stated to set objectives, methodology, timetable and the agricultural sample size, none of which is published; preparation has now been validated twice in four weeks without an enumeration date being fixed ([earlier validation](2026-07-28-ahoraeg-inege-validacion-censos)).

summary: [Data collection for an extractive-industries transparency report](2026-07-30-inicia-en-malabo-taller-recopilacion-datos-informe-eiti-guinea-ecuatorial-2024) opened in July 2026, the last outstanding measure before an international programme validation.
developments:
No report has been published ([data collection](2026-07-30-inicia-en-malabo-taller-recopilacion-datos-informe-eiti-guinea-ecuatorial-2024)).

No national open data portal, policy or dataset inventory exists anywhere in the base, so a single sector report driven by an external validation deadline is the entire open-data record.

summary: A [technology cooperation roadmap](2025-06-17-china-apoyo-desarrollo-tecnologico-ahoraeg) aims to make the country a regional technology hub, and the state operator signed a network contract with a Chinese vendor in July 2026.
developments:
The roadmap names institute training and a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence forum at the new capital, with no delivery, disbursement or completion figure on record ([roadmap](2025-06-17-china-apoyo-desarrollo-tecnologico-ahoraeg)).

The operator's modernisation programme covers fifth-generation networks, embedded subscriber modules, public wireless access and fibre reactivation on that contract, signed on 9 July 2026 ([contract](2026-07-10-getesa-huawei-alianza-red-reg), [programme](2026-05-25-getesa-modernizacion-5g-wifi-getesa-money-reg)); the independent press reports opaque procurement and overlapping state operators around it.

The same vendor is behind the substation fibre proposal and was met by the infrastructure operator's new leadership within a fortnight of its appointment, so one supplier stands behind the network, the grid proposal and the training pipeline.
